paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: your word matters to the LORD. Moses opens with a man who makes a vow to the LORD, and the command is plain: "he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised." (Numbers 30:2) That means every "I promise," from the big ones to the little ones, is something the LORD takes seriously. I've said "I'll be right back" and then disappeared into a junk drawer for years, so believe me, I know how easy it is to say a thing too fast!

Now look at what the rest of the passage does. It walks through a young woman in her father's house, a wife in her husband's house, and a widow or divorced woman, and it says what happens to a vow in each situation. I'm not going to say why the command is set up this way, because the text doesn't say. What I can say is that the LORD cared about the vows of every one of them, and He wrote down what to do in each case. Even when a father or husband prohibits a vow, the text says "the LORD will absolve her." (Numbers 30:5)

So what do you take to your own kitchen? Think before you promise, because a vow is not a throwaway line. When a promise lands on you, keep it, and when you can't, don't go quiet and let it rot. Hear it from me, the stamper who stays ready for the Supper: a baker whose word is good is a baker the LORD can build on!
